An unqualified denial that any discourse imperative stands between the header and the rubric therefore cannot survive a form standing inside the row's own splice, and that arm of the warrant sentence is defective. The other arm is not contradicted and the challenge does not separate them: the addressee at 30:2 is the figure the header itself names, הַדָּבָר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָיָ֣ה אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ (oshb:Jer.30.1, byte), so nothing NEW is addressed — the address is specified, not reopened — and the messenger formula at 30:2 carries no frame-owner change, the mouth being the same throughout. Under the ruled internal-seam classes a commissioning write-command inside a superscription is not the audience-summoning discourse frame that cuts, so the seam stands, as the challenge itself concedes. One further check the challenge did not make: the row's narrower version of the same absence, made in strongest_rejected_alternative about the 30:3/30:4 turn, is byte-true — MT 30:4 carries no speech formula, no imperative and no second-person form (oshb:Jer.30.4, byte). docket.grounds: Both upheld; distinct defects, one mechanical and one substantive. (i) The 30:5 pair splices the whole verse including כִּי כֹה֙ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.30.5, byte) but glosses only from the cry onward, while the staged verse opens “For Yahweh says:” (web:Jer.30.5) — the formula's own English stands in the same staged verse and is left uncovered, on the single device the row cites as its opening warrant. A flat denial that any addressee change marks that turn is byte-false. Two calibration points that do not disturb the finding but do bear on how strong the rival is. First, that marking is sustained to the row's own close, וְאַתָּ֡ה אַל תִּירָא֩ עַבְדִּ֨י (oshb:Jer.30.10, byte) and כִּֽי אִתְּךָ֥ אֲנִ֛י through אֲנַקֶּֽךָּ (oshb:Jer.30.11, byte for each), so this is a turn into a sustained address rather than a one-verse anomaly. A precision note on the framing, not a correction to the finding: the flagged word in that sentence is a restrictive adverb and is a genuine keyword false positive on its own terms; what fails is the absence clause standing beside it. Everything else verifies: no mark at MT 30:4, SAMEKH at MT 30:9, PE at MT 30:11, one paseq seg each at MT 30:8 and MT 30:11 (single-witness, count-only), no ketiv/qere; the hoy at 30:7 is the day-alas role and not a woe onset; the Jacob spelling is defective at 30:7 and twice at 30:10 (sweep: 2 token hits at Jer.30.10, 1 prefixed at Jer.30.7, skeleton, finals-normalized) against the plene form at 30:18; and all five pointed runs and all five English runs are byte-true and verbatim respectively.

It is even the time of Jacob’s trouble; but he will be saved out of it.” (web:Jer.30.7) — an exclamation over the day's own severity rather than a pronounced judgment against a named party, closing already on the promise of rescue rather than on threat alone. The rescue promise continues through the same defective spelling of Jacob's name twice over, וְאַתָּ֡ה אַל תִּירָא֩ עַבְדִּ֨י יַעֲקֹ֤ב נְאֻם יְהֹוָה֙ וְאַל תֵּחַ֣ת יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל כִּ֠י הִנְנִ֤י מוֹשִֽׁיעֲךָ֙ מֵֽרָח֔וֹק וְאֶֽת זַרְעֲךָ֖ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ שִׁבְיָ֑ם וְשָׁ֧ב יַעֲקֹ֛ב וְשָׁקַ֥ט וְשַׁאֲנַ֖ן וְאֵ֥ין מַחֲרִֽיד (oshb:Jer.30.10, byte), matching “Therefore don’t be afraid, O Jacob my servant, says Yahweh. Don’t be dismayed, Israel. For, behold, I will save you from afar, and save your offspring from the land of their captivity. Jacob will return, and will be quiet and at ease. No one will make him afraid.” (web:Jer.30.10). It closes on כִּֽי אִתְּךָ֥ אֲנִ֛י נְאֻם יְהוָ֖ה לְהֽוֹשִׁיעֶ֑ךָ כִּי֩ אֶעֱשֶׂ֨ה כָלָ֜ה בְּכָֽל הַגּוֹיִ֣ם אֲשֶׁ֧ר הֲפִצוֹתִ֣יךָ שָּׁ֗ם אַ֤ךְ אֹֽתְךָ֙ לֹֽא אֶעֱשֶׂ֣ה כָלָ֔ה וְיִסַּרְתִּ֨יךָ֙ לַמִּשְׁפָּ֔ט וְנַקֵּ֖ה לֹ֥א אֲנַקֶּֽךָּ (oshb:Jer.30.11, byte), matching “For I am with you, says Yahweh, to save you; for I will make a full end of all the nations where I have scattered you, but I will not make a full end of you; but I will correct you in measure, and will in no way leave you unpunished.” (web:Jer.30.11). (i) The 30:12 pair splices the whole verse including כִּ֣י כֹ֥ה אָמַ֛ר יְהוָ֖ה (oshb:Jer.30.12, byte) but glosses only from the wound complaint onward, while the staged verse opens “For Yahweh says,” (web:Jer.30.12); the 30:17 pair splices the whole verse including כִּי֩ אַעֲלֶ֨ה אֲרֻכָ֥ה לָ֛ךְ וּמִמַּכּוֹתַ֥יִךְ אֶרְפָּאֵ֖ךְ נְאֻם יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.30.17, byte) but glosses only the outcast clause, leaving “For I will restore health to you, and I will heal you of your wounds,” (web:Jer.30.17) uncovered. Both are real, and the 30:17 gap is load-bearing twice: the healing clause is the content the row's own close rests on AND the content its rejection of the judgment reading rests on, and both lenses reached that verse independently. (ii) The object is mis-anchored. The digits reproduce exactly on an independent re-sweep of the consonantal skeleton — the token stands in 55 verses book-wide and verse-initially in exactly 2 across MT chs 29-31, MT 29:32 and MT 30:16 (sweep: 2 verses, verse-initial, finals-normalized) — and לָכֵ֞ן (oshb:Jer.30.16, byte) does stand verse-initially at the joint. What survives is narrower and still a defect: the sentence names no swept object before asserting the absence, and the pivot particle at 30:16 is a byte-true hinge sitting at the exact joint the rejection concerns and goes undisclosed. A byte fact neither reading drew: because that particle turns the announcement at 30:16 rather than at 30:17, it argues the reversal begins one verse earlier than the rejected complaint-only grouping of 30:12-30:16 assumes, so it tells against that alternative rather than for it.
